posted.title: Comment#draft fetches draft without tenant scoping
posted.details:
**summary:** **What's wrong:** `Comment#draft` queries `DraftTask` by id only. `TenantScoped` adds no default scope, so this can load a draft belonging to a different company, and `CommentBlueprint` then serializes its `title`, `state`, and `points`.

**When it happens:** `Comments::Commands::Create` permits `draft_task_id` from request params, so a client can store a foreign draft id; the comment's API response then leaks that draft's data.

**Fix:** Scope the lookup to the comment's tenant:
```ruby
DraftTask.where(id: draft_task_id, company_id: company_id).first if draft_task_id
```

posted.title: Attach happy path is stubbed and untested
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** The example stubs `DraftTasks::Commands::Attach`, so no attachment ever happens, and the stub has no `with(...)`, so the controller's arguments go unchecked too. Only the echoed `id` is asserted — this is the only stubbed command call in `spec/requests`.

**When it happens:** If the controller passed the wrong `list_id`, or the command broke, this test still passes.

**Fix:** Drop the stub and assert the outcome, e.g. `expect(json["list_id"]).to eq(list.id.to_s)` and `expect(draft.reload.list_id).to eq(list.id)`.

label.title: Attach request spec stubs the command so it passes with no attach
label.label: nit
label.note: the 'attaches the draft to the list' example stubs DraftTasks::Commands::Attach.call to return Result.success(draft) and asserts 200 and the id, so it would pass if the controller never attached anything; the command spec covers behaviour, the request spec only covers routing/authorization

posted.title: Destroy policy change lacks test coverage
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `destroy?` now permits destroying any list that is not soft-deleted, dropping the old archived-only guard, but nothing tests the new rule — no policy spec is updated and the modified lists request spec contains no destroy cases.

**When it happens:** A later edit re-requires `archived?` or re-allows destroying already-deleted lists, and the full suite still passes.

**Fix:** Add specs: an owner/admin can destroy an active, non-archived list; an already soft-deleted list is rejected.

posted.title: Swallowed comment failure permanently drops the draft note
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** Any comment failure — validation errors raised by `.value!`, or transient DB errors — is silently swallowed. The draft was already marked sent by `SendDraft`, so the note is never retried and the author is never notified (the job only notifies on failure results).

**When it happens:** `ConvertDraftTasksJob` converts a draft whose comment fails to save, e.g. a validation or database error during `Comments::Commands::Create`.

**Fix:** Handle `Result.failure` explicitly — retry or notify the author — instead of returning `nil`, and log at `error` level.

label.title: Note comment failure is swallowed after the draft is already sent
label.label: real
label.note: build_comment rescues StandardError from Comments::Commands::Create.value! (for example a note longer than Comment::MAX_BODY, which DraftTask does not validate), logs and returns nil; the task exists and the draft is sent, so the job cannot retry and the user sees a sent draft with its note missing

posted.title: Deleted-list guard lacks test coverage
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `Attach` refuses deleted lists with a distinct failure ("list ... has been deleted"), but this spec never exercises that branch. Every other guard — archived, foreign company, sent state, non-author — has a case in this file.

**When it happens:** Someone refactors `Attach` and drops or breaks the `list.deleted?` check; no spec fails, and drafts can be attached to deleted lists.

**Fix:** Add a case mirroring the archived one: attach to a deleted list and assert the deleted failure.

posted.title: Author name field causes N+1 on public pages
posted.details:
**summary:** **What's wrong:** `task.author.display_name` lazily loads each task's author record. `Sharing::Queries::PublicList#tasks` builds tasks via `list.tasks.not_archived.ordered.to_a` with no `includes(:author)`, so every task adds one extra SQL query.

**When it happens:** Any public share page request whose list has tasks — 30 tasks triggers 30 extra `User` queries per request, on unauthenticated traffic.

**Fix:** Preload the association where tasks are loaded, e.g. `list.tasks.not_archived.ordered.includes(:author)`, and do the same for the search results passed to this blueprint.

**confidence_note:** Verified the public list query performs no eager loading of authors.

posted.title: Author name serialized twice in public payload
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** the same value is rendered twice in this brand-new public payload: flat `author_name` (via `fields`) and nested `author: { name: ... }`. Consumers get two keys for one datum, and the public contract must now keep both in sync forever.

**When it happens:** every draft in the share-page JSON contains both `"author_name"` and `"author": {"name": ...}` with identical values.

**Fix:** keep exactly one form — drop `author_name` from `fields`, or drop the `author` block.

posted.title: Notification creation result is silently ignored
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `notify_failure` discards the `Result` returned by `Notifications::Commands::Create`, which fails when the recipient is not a company member or the notification record is invalid.

**When it happens:** A draft's author was removed from the company, then their draft fails conversion; the notification is skipped with no log line or error.

**Fix:** Capture the result and log failures, mirroring how the conversion result is handled in `perform`:

```ruby
result = Notifications::Commands::Create.call(...)
logger.warn("draft #{draft.id} notification not created: #{result.error}") if result.failure?
```

posted.title: Mid-run failure makes cleanup permanently unretryable
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** The list is marked deleted before the cleanup runs. If a later step raises, the run stops half-done, and retrying hits the `list.deleted?` guard and returns failure — the leftover cleanup never happens.

**When it happens:** `revoke!` raises after `update!` saved; the next call short-circuits with "already deleted", so drafts, draft comments and active share links stay on the deleted list.

**Fix:** Run the idempotent cleanup before `update!(deleted_at: ...)`, or wrap the body in a DB transaction.

posted.title: New count fields add three queries per list
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `member_count` calls `list.members`, a non-memoized method that issues two queries (`draft_tasks.attached.not_sent.distinct(:author_id)` plus a `User` count). `attached_draft_count` then runs the same `attached.not_sent` filter a third time.

**When it happens:** `GET /api/v1/lists` renders every list with `:with_counts`, so each list now fires ~5 count queries (previously 2); 50 lists means roughly 250 queries per request.

**Fix:** Memoize `List#members`/`attached_author_ids`, or compute all counts in one aggregation inside the `ListLists` query and pass them to the blueprint.

posted.title: Comment collections fire one query per draft
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `Comment#draft` runs a separate `DraftTask` query every time it is called. The blueprint is rendered with `render_collection` on comment index endpoints, so a thread of N attached-draft comments now costs 1 + N queries.

**When it happens:** `GET /api/v1/lists/:id/comments` (or the tasks equivalent) returns many "attached a draft" comments; each one triggers its own `DraftTask.where(...)` lookup.

**Fix:** Batch-load once — e.g. build a `DraftTask.in(id: draft_task_ids)` map in the comments query and pass it via blueprint options — instead of calling `comment.draft` per comment.

label.title: Comment list loads the draft once per comment
label.label: nit
label.note: the draft field calls comment.draft (DraftTask.where(id:).first) for each comment rendered; the comments index is paginated (25 default, 100 max) and only attach comments have draft_task_id, so it is a bounded N+1 off the hot path

held_back.title: Destroy returns success without deleting comment
held_back.details:
**What's wrong:** When the comment holds a draft, deletion is delegated to `DraftTasks::Commands::Detach`. If the draft is not attached (or is attached to a different list), `Detach` succeeds without deleting any comment, yet `Destroy` still reports success.

**When it happens:** The comment's `draft_task_id` references a draft whose `list` is nil or another list. The API answers success and the comment stays visible.

**Fix:** After a successful detach, remove the comment explicitly (idempotent):

```ruby
result = DraftTasks::Commands::Detach.call(draft: draft, actor: actor)
return result if result.failure?

Comment.where(id: comment.id).delete_all
Result.success(comment)
```

posted.title: Public author field leaks private draft author names
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** The `author` field reads `view.draft.author.name` directly, bypassing the privacy guard in `DraftPublicView`, which sets `author_name` to nil for private drafts and uses `display_name` (with email fallback). The public payload can expose the real author name anyway.

**When it happens:** A visitor opens a share page whose list has a draft where `private?` is true: `author_name` renders null but `author.name` shows the real name (plus the author id).

**Fix:** Use the view's guarded value instead of the raw association:

```ruby
field :author do |view|
  view.author_name && { id: view.draft.author_id.to_s, name: view.author_name }
end
```

label.label: real

posted.title: Draft is created after the job already ran
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `draft` is a lazy `let` from the shared context, and in this example it is first referenced only after `perform`. So the list contains just `broken` while the job runs.

**When it happens:** Running this spec: the job never sees `draft`, so `expect(draft.reload).to be_sent` fails — the draft is created at that line, still `ready`.

**Fix:** Force creation before `perform`, as the archived-list example does (the first example needs it too):

```ruby
draft
broken = create(:draft_task, :ready, company: company, list: list, author: member)
```

posted.title: Swallowed comment failures silently drop draft notes
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** Every comment failure is swallowed: `.value!` raises on the failure Results that `Comments::Commands::Create` returns (and on real bugs), and the rescue hides all of it at warn level.

**When it happens:** A ready draft converts and comment creation fails — the draft is already `sent`, so the task ships without its note, and `ConvertDraftTasksJob` skips its `draft_conversion_failed` author notification because the command still returns success.

**Fix:** At minimum log at `error`; better, return a failure Result from `call` so `notify_failure` informs the author.

posted.title: Soft-deleted lists keep their unique slug
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** Deleting now only stamps `deleted_at`; the document stays in the collection and keeps its `slug`, so the unique index on `{ company_id, slug }` still counts the tombstone and that slug stays taken forever.

**When it happens:** A user deletes the "Marketing" list, then later creates a new "Marketing" list. Slug generation collides with the invisible deleted document: creation fails with a duplicate-key/uniqueness error, or the new list gets a suffixed slug even though no visible list uses that name.

**Fix:** Use a partial unique index (`partialFilterExpression: { deleted_at: null }`), scope slug-uniqueness checks to `not_deleted`, or clear/rename the slug when soft-deleting.

posted.title: author_name field triggers N+1 user queries
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** The new field calls `task.author.display_name` for every task, but no call site preloads `author` (no `includes`/`preload` exists in `app/`). Each task triggers one extra `User` query.

**When it happens:** The public share page and the search endpoint render this blueprint; a list with 50 tasks fires ~50 extra queries per page view.

**Fix:** Preload authors where the tasks collection is loaded, e.g. `tasks.includes(:author)` in both the public list query and the search controller.

posted.title: Rendering comments fires one DraftTask query each
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `draft` runs a fresh `DraftTask.where(id: ...)` query on every call, and `CommentBlueprint` calls it once per rendered comment — a classic N+1.

**When it happens:** A request renders a comment list where several comments have `draft_task_id` set; each one triggers its own query.

**Fix:** Replace the raw field with `belongs_to :draft_task, optional: true` (drop the manual field and method) and render collections with `Comment.includes(:draft_task)`.

label.label: nit
label.note: the draft field calls comment.draft (DraftTask.where(id:).first) for each comment rendered; the comments index is paginated (25 default, 100 max) and only attach comments have draft_task_id, so it is a bounded N+1 off the hot path

posted.title: Draft author assertion compares wrong attribute
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `DraftPublicView` renders `author.display_name`, but this expectation compares the payload value to `member.name`. The sibling task assertion correctly uses `admin.display_name`.

**When it happens:** The test only passes because both values happen to match for factory users; if `display_name` falls back to email or differs from `name`, the expectation no longer matches what the endpoint returns.

**Fix:** Assert the attribute actually rendered:
```ruby
expect(json["drafts"].first["author"]["name"]).to eq(member.display_name)
```

posted.title: Index runs five count queries per list
posted.details:
**summary:** **What's wrong:** `ListsController#index` renders the `with_counts` view for every list, and each added field runs its own Mongo query; `member_count` alone costs two (`draft_tasks.attached.not_sent.distinct(:author_id)` plus a `User` count).

**When it happens:** A company with 100 lists triggers roughly 500 queries to render the index response.

**Fix:** Batch the counts in one aggregate grouped by `list_id`, or memoize the shared `attached.not_sent` criteria on the list.

posted.title: member_count and member_ids count different people
posted.details:
**summary:** **What's wrong:** `member_count` uses `list.members`, which merges stored `member_ids` with authors of attached, unsent drafts. The base `member_ids` field only exposes the stored ids, so the same response can show 1 member id but a count of 3.

**When it happens:** A list with one stored member and an attached draft written by another user renders `member_ids: ["<owner>"]` yet `member_count: 2`.

**Fix:** Count the same set you expose, e.g. `list.member_ids.size`, or rename the field (e.g. `effective_member_count`) if the wider set is intended.

posted.title: Attached guard misses deleted lists, diverging from SendDraft
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `attached?` only checks `list_id.present?`, but the sibling `SendDraft` command treats a draft on a deleted list as not attached, raising the same `DraftTasks::NotAttached` error from a different condition.

**When it happens:** A draft sits on a soft-deleted list: `mark_ready` passes this guard, marks it ready and reserves its points, yet `send_draft` then always fails — the draft is stuck in `ready` with points held.

**Fix:** Share one predicate, e.g. make `attached?` also require `!list.deleted?`, and call it from both commands.

posted.title: Attach-comment deletion query duplicated across commands
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** The query that finds and deletes a draft's attach comment is copy-pasted from `Attach#replace_attach_comment`. The rule "an attach comment is a `List` comment tagged with `draft_task_id`" is now encoded in two commands.

**When it happens:** If how attach comments are stored ever changes (e.g. a different `commentable_type`), both sites must be updated in sync; missing one leaves stale comments on the list after detaching.

**Fix:** Extract a `Comment` scope such as `attach_comment_for(draft, list_id)` and call it from both `Attach` and `Detach`.

```ruby
Comment.attach_comment_for(locked, previous_list_id).delete_all
```

posted.title: Failed attach leaves draft attached, comment missing
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** The draft is persisted before its attach comment is replaced. If `Comments::Commands::Create` fails, `.value!` raises after the old comment was already deleted, leaving the draft attached with no comment.

**When it happens:** Comment creation fails once; a retry hits the `draft.list_id == list.id` early return, so the attach comment is never recreated.

**Fix:** Create the new comment before updating the draft, and delete the old comment only after both succeed.

posted.title: Destroy returns success without deleting comment
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `Detach` returns an early success when the draft is not `attached?` and deletes no comments, but `release_draft` then returns success unconditionally — a "destroyed" comment can still exist.

**When it happens:** The list comment references a live draft whose `attached?` is false (e.g. a flow that un-attaches without cleaning up comments); the API reports deleted, but the comment stays and can never be removed via this command.

**Fix:** Guarantee removal after detaching:

```ruby
comment.destroy! if Comment.where(id: comment.id).exists?
```

posted.title: Feature flag subject mismatch breaks mark_ready rollout
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `mark_ready?` checks `Features.enabled?(:draft_tasks, user)`, which matches the user's email against the flag's `users` list. The controller gate `require_feature!(:draft_tasks)` checks `current_company` against `companies` slugs. Same flag, two different subjects.

**When it happens:** Production enables `draft_tasks` only via `companies: [acme, northwind]` with no `users`. Acme users pass the controller gate, but `mark_ready?` is always false, so the whole draft-to-send flow 403s for every rollout company. Specs miss it because `enable_feature(:draft_tasks)` turns on `everyone`.

**Fix:** Use the same subject as the controller:

```ruby
same_company? && author? && record.drafting? && Features.enabled?(:draft_tasks, record.company)
```

or drop the check, since the controller's `before_action` already gates this action.

label.title: Policy and controller check the flag against different subjects
label.label: real
label.note: `mark_ready?` adds `Features.enabled?(:draft_tasks, user)` while RequiresFeature checks `Features.enabled?(:draft_tasks, current_company)`. Features matches a Company by slug and a User by email, so a flag rolled out with `companies:` (the production config) passes the controller and fails the policy: mark_ready is a 403 for every pilot company. Specs enable the flag with `everyone: true` so they do not see it.

posted.title: Draft can be converted twice, creating duplicate tasks
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `SendDraft` creates the task while holding the draft's Redis lock, but the lock is released before `mark_sent!` runs here. Another request still sees the draft as `ready` and creates a second task.

**When it happens:** Double-clicking the convert action, or `build_comment` raising via `.value!` after the task was already created and the user retries.

**Fix:** Run comment creation, `mark_sent!` and the notification inside the locked section, e.g. by passing a callback/block to `SendDraft`.

label.title: mark_sent! runs after the lock is released
label.label: real
label.note: ConvertDraftTaskComment calls SendDraft with `finalize: false` (task created under WithLockedDraft) and then calls `draft.mark_sent!(task)` after the block has returned the lock. A release that claims ready -> drafting in between makes the claim in `mark_sent!` raise WrongState: the task exists, points are spent, and the draft is back in drafting where it can be marked ready and sent again.

posted.title: Shared lock service raises SendDraft-scoped error
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** The generic `WithLockedDraft` service now raises `DraftTasks::Commands::SendDraft::Lock::Busy`, a class owned by one specific command. `MarkReady` and `Release` use this same service, so their lock failures raise and rescue an error named after `SendDraft`, and the service layer depends on a command namespace.

**When it happens:** Lock contention while running `MarkReady` or `Release` — the error object is `SendDraft::Lock::Busy`, misattributing the failure and breaking if `SendDraft` is renamed.

**Fix:** Move the class to the shared error home, e.g. `DraftTasks::LockBusy < DraftTasks::Error` in `draft_tasks/errors.rb`, and update all raise/rescue sites.

label.title: Lock::Busy lives in the Send command but is raised by the lock service
label.label: nit
label.note: WithLockedDraft raises `DraftTasks::Commands::SendDraft::Lock::Busy`, which MarkReady and Release also rescue, so the error class is owned by one command but shared by three callers and the lock service. Behaviour is correct; this is placement.

posted.title: Limit keeps oldest 50 comments, drops newest
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `chronological` orders comments oldest-first, so `.limit(LIMIT)` returns the 50 *oldest* comments and silently drops every comment added after that. Users can never see the latest ones. The sibling `Comments::Queries::ListComments` has no cap at all.

**When it happens:** The sent task has 51+ comments; the draft comments endpoint renders only the first 50, so the newest comments are invisible.

**Fix:** Take the newest 50, then present them oldest-first:

```ruby
Comment.where(commentable_type: "Task", commentable_id: draft.sent_task_id)
       .order(created_at: :desc).limit(LIMIT).reverse
```

Update the "caps the list" spec to assert the newest comments are kept.

posted.title: One failing draft blocks all scheduled sends
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** Re-raising inside `send_one` stops the whole loop, so a draft that keeps failing blocks every draft after it. After Sidekiq's 3 retries the job dies and no scheduled sends happen at all.

**When it happens:** One draft's Mongo write fails persistently, e.g. a duplicate-key `OperationFailure`; each retry run stops at that draft and the drafts behind it are never sent.

**Fix:** Log and continue instead of re-raising — the failed draft stays in the `ready` scope, so the next scheduled run retries it:

posted.title: New ReadOnlyKeys error has no test coverage
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `ReadOnlyKeys` is raised when a client tries to set protected params, but no spec in the repo references the class, its message, or its `draft_tasks.errors.read_only` translation key.

**When it happens:** A `PATCH` sending a read-only param (e.g. `state`) must be rejected; if the guard regresses, no test fails and clients could silently overwrite protected fields.

**Fix:** Add a request spec that submits a read-only param and asserts the error status and message.

posted.title: Failed replacement still deletes the old recording
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `ReplaceAttachment` destroys the draft's current recording before validating the new upload. On rejection the old recording is already gone and `attachment_id` dangles, but this test only checks the failure.

**When it happens:** A draft that already has a recording receives an upload above `MEDIA_MAX_BYTES`; the command returns failure after `draft.attachment&.destroy` already ran.

**Fix:** Assert the old recording survives, and in the command destroy it only after the new upload validates.

label.title: Old recording is removed before the new upload is validated
label.label: nit
label.note: `draft.attachment&.destroy` runs before `attachment.update(draft_task_id: ...)`, so a media-limit validation failure on the new upload leaves the draft with no recording. Only reachable when an over-limit media file got past the client's pre-upload check, and the PR body states it as a deliberate tradeoff with a follow-up.

posted.title: Concurrent drafts can claim the same attachment
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `claimed?` is read before `draft_task_id` is written in a separate `update`, so two requests can both see "unclaimed" and both claim the attachment; both drafts then point at one attachment owned by only one of them, and the unconditional `draft.attachment&.destroy` can later delete a recording another record now owns.

**When it happens:** The same fresh upload is attached to two different drafts at nearly the same time; both pass the `claimed?` check inside the race window.

**Fix:** Claim atomically like `DraftTask#claim!` does: `Attachment.where(id: attachment.id, draft_task_id: nil, task_id: nil).find_one_and_update({ "$set" => { draft_task_id: draft.id } })` and treat a `nil` result as `:claimed`.

posted.title: Un-prefixed Tasks:: constant can NameError at load
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `Tasks::Blueprints::TaskBlueprint` lacks the leading `::` that this same diff adds to the `DraftTasks::` constants. Ruby resolves a bare `Tasks` through the enclosing `Api::V1` scope, and a `Tasks` module already exists there (`app/controllers/api/v1/tasks/comments_controller.rb`), so it can resolve to `Api::V1::Tasks` instead of the top-level `Tasks`.

**When it happens:** If `Api::V1::Tasks` is loaded before this controller loads (order-dependent), the class-body lookup raises `NameError: uninitialized constant Api::V1::Tasks::Blueprints`, breaking every draft-task request.

**Fix:** Prefix the constant path:

```ruby
TASK_BLUEPRINT = ::Tasks::Blueprints::TaskBlueprint
```

posted.title: Oversized attachment fails validation at create
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `Attachment` validates `byte_size` against `MEDIA_MAX_BYTES` whenever the file is audio or video, including on create. This record is therefore invalid, so `create` raises `Mongoid::Errors::Validations` and the example never reaches the command.

**When it happens:** Running the suite; the factory tries to persist a 10 MB + 1 byte audio upload.

**Fix:** Persist without validations, e.g. `upload = build(...); upload.save(validate: false)`.

posted.title: Draft-claimed attachments are never tested as claimed
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `claimed?` is true when `task_id` or `draft_task_id` is set, but the test only asserts the task case. The draft branch that `ReplaceAttachment` relies on to reject already-claimed recordings is untested.

**When it happens:** If `draft_task_id.present?` is dropped from `claimed?`, this spec still passes and one recording could be attached to two drafts.

**Fix:** Add `expect(build(:attachment, :unclaimed, draft_task_id: BSON::ObjectId.new)).to be_claimed`.

posted.title: Task stores draft link twice, index unused
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** The draft→task link is now stored in two places: `Task#draft_task_id` and the existing `DraftTask#sent_task_id`. Nothing queries tasks by `draft_task_id`, so the new sparse index only adds write overhead, and the two copies can drift.

**When it happens:** `SendDraft` creates the task with `draft_task_id`, then `mark_sent!` separately writes `sent_task_id`; if `mark_sent!` fails or `finalize: false`, only one side is set.

**Fix:** Drop both lines and read the link via `draft.sent_task`, or keep a single direction.

posted.title: Duplicate size validations produce conflicting errors
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** Two separate `validates :byte_size` lines both run for media files. An oversized video fails both, so `errors[:byte_size]` gets two contradictory messages ("must be less than or equal to 26214400" and "... 10485760").

**When it happens:** Uploading any audio or video file larger than `MAX_BYTES` (25 MB); `attachment.errors.full_messages` then returns both size errors to the client.

**Fix:** Make the two validations mutually exclusive so only one runs per record:

```ruby
validates :byte_size, numericality: { greater_than: 0, less_than_or_equal_to: MAX_BYTES }, unless: :media?
validates :byte_size, numericality: { greater_than: 0, less_than_or_equal_to: MEDIA_MAX_BYTES }, if: :media?
```

posted.title: Concurrent edits write the same revision
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `draft.revision + 1` is read from the in-memory copy and written with a plain `$set`. If two edits run at the same time, both read the same revision and both persist the same next number, so the counter silently loses an increment.

**When it happens:** Two requests edit the same draft concurrently, e.g. a double-submit or two browser tabs.

**Fix:** Let MongoDB increment it atomically: drop `revision` from the `set` hash and use `draft.inc(revision: 1)` (a `$inc` update).

posted.title: Failed edits still release the draft
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `resume_drafting!` saves the new state before the edits are checked. If `locked.update(edits)` fails, the draft is already back in `drafting` with its reservation freed, yet a failure is returned.

**When it happens:** Releasing a `ready` draft with an invalid `note` or `scheduled_for` shows an error, but the draft actually moved; retrying then hits the `drafting?` early-return and silently drops the edits.

**Fix:** Validate first, then transition once, mirroring `MarkReady`:

```ruby
locked.assign_attributes(edits)
return Result.failure(locked.errors.full_messages) unless locked.valid?
locked.resume_drafting!
```

posted.title: Attachment field causes N+1 queries on index
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** The new `attachment` field calls `draft.attachment`, which runs a separate `Attachment.where(id: ...)` query for each draft. The `index` action renders a whole collection through this blueprint, so every draft with an attachment adds one extra DB query.

**When it happens:** `GET /api/v1/draft_tasks` returning 50 drafts with attachments fires roughly 50 extra queries on top of the list query.

**Fix:** Batch-load attachments once (e.g. `Attachment.in(id: ids)` mapped by `attachment_id` in `ListDrafts`) and render from that map, or memoize the lookup.

posted.title: Serializer queries DraftTask once per comment
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** The `draft` block calls `DraftTask.find` for every from-draft comment — a DB query inside the serializer. It also raises `Mongoid::Errors::DocumentNotFound` if the referenced draft no longer exists, failing the whole comments response.

**When it happens:** Listing comments where several carry `draft_task_id` (a bare field with no association, so nothing nullifies it after a draft is deleted).

**Fix:** Batch-load drafts in `ListDraftComments` (`DraftTask.where(:_id.in => ids)`) and pass the map via render `options`; return `nil` when a draft is missing.

label.title: Per-comment DraftTask.find in the comments blueprint
label.label: nit
label.note: The `draft` field does `DraftTask.find(comment.draft_task_id)` per comment. The list is capped at ListDraftComments::LIMIT (50) and in practice one comment per task comes from a draft, so this is a handful of extra reads on a cold endpoint, not something to block on.

posted.title: Duplicated `draft` helper across three controllers
posted.details:
**text:** **What's wrong:** The `draft` memoized finder is copy-pasted verbatim into `CommentsController` and `AttachmentsController`, with a near-identical variant in `DraftTasksController` (only the param key differs). The `DraftTaskScoped` concern added in this same PR is the natural shared home for it.

**When it happens:** Any future change to draft lookup (scoping, soft-delete handling, error behavior) must now be repeated in three controllers and can silently diverge.

**Fix:** Define it once in `DraftTaskScoped`:

```ruby
def draft
  @draft ||= draft_tasks.find(params[:draft_task_id] || params[:id])
end
```

and delete the three per-controller copies.

posted.title: Hand-rolled failure rendering bypasses shared result helper
posted.details:
**summary:** **What's wrong:** Every sibling command action in this controller family renders results through the shared `render_result` helper (see `DraftTasksController#update`), but this action re-implements failure handling locally. Exception failures are re-raised into `HandlesErrors` (body `{error: {code, message}}`), while string/array failures render `{errors: [...]}` — two different error body shapes from the same endpoint.

**When it happens:** A non-author calling the endpoint gets `"only the author can change the recording"` as `{errors: [...]}`; a non-editable draft gets `DraftTasks::NotEditable` re-raised and rendered as `{error: {...}}` by the global handler.

**Fix:** Reuse `render_result(result, blueprint: BLUEPRINT)` like `DraftTasksController#update`, or extract this failure branch into the shared base so all endpoints share one error format.

**word_count:** 95

posted.title: Budget-short mark_ready 422 lost its request test
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** The "budget is short" request test was deleted. `Commands::MarkReady` still returns `Points::InsufficientBalance`, but only the command unit spec covers it — the API's 422 response for exhausted points is untested.

**When it happens:** The author's giving balance cannot cover the draft's points and the error mapping regresses; clients get a wrong status instead of 422.

**Fix:** Restore the removed scenario (a second ready draft exhausting the balance).

posted.title: Draft marked sent outside the send lock
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `SendDraft` releases its Redis lock before returning, and `draft.mark_sent!(task)` now runs after that, so the ready→sent state flip is no longer atomic with task creation.

**When it happens:** If `build_comment` raises (its `.value!` fails) or the process dies, the task exists but the draft is still `ready`; a retry creates a duplicate task. A concurrent send in that window can also double-send.

**Fix:** Run comment creation and finalization inside `SendDraft`'s locked block, e.g. via an `on_finalize` callback, so state and task change together.

label.title: mark_sent! runs after the lock is released
label.label: real
label.note: ConvertDraftTaskComment calls SendDraft with `finalize: false` (task created under WithLockedDraft) and then calls `draft.mark_sent!(task)` after the block has returned the lock. A release that claims ready -> drafting in between makes the claim in `mark_sent!` raise WrongState: the task exists, points are spent, and the draft is back in drafting where it can be marked ready and sent again.

posted.title: Failed replace still deletes the old recording
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** The draft's current recording is destroyed before the new attachment is saved. If that save fails, the old recording is already gone and `draft.attachment_id` still points to the deleted record.

**When it happens:** An author replaces the recording with an upload that fails validation, e.g. media larger than `MEDIA_MAX_BYTES`; the command returns failure but the previous recording was destroyed.

**Fix:** Reorder: run `attachment.update(draft_task_id: draft.id)` first, and only destroy `draft.attachment` after it succeeds.

label.title: Old recording is removed before the new upload is validated
label.label: nit
label.note: `draft.attachment&.destroy` runs before `attachment.update(draft_task_id: ...)`, so a media-limit validation failure on the new upload leaves the draft with no recording. Only reachable when an over-limit media file got past the client's pre-upload check, and the PR body states it as a deliberate tradeoff with a follow-up.

posted.title: Release races with send, corrupts draft state
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** Release dropped the draft lock and the atomic `resume_drafting!` transition. The `sent?` check and the later `update` are not atomic, so another process can change state in between.

**When it happens:** A ready draft is released while `SendDraft` (which still locks) sends it; the unconditional `update(state: "drafting")` then flips the sent draft back and clears `points_reserved_at`.

**Fix:** Restore `WithLockedDraft` and `locked.resume_drafting!`, as `mark_ready` and `send_draft` still do.

label.title: Release overwrites a concurrent send
label.label: real
label.note: At the early push Release does not take WithLockedDraft and ends with `draft.update(state: "drafting", ready_at: nil, points_reserved_at: nil)` with no state filter; a send that lands between the `draft.sent?` check and the update is overwritten, leaving a draft in drafting with a task already created and points spent. Head uses `resume_drafting!`, a filtered claim on state "ready", under the lock.

posted.title: Draft destroy lacks tests for attachment cleanup
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** The command now deletes the draft's attachment, but the PR adds no spec for this behavior. Every other command changed in this PR (`mark_ready`, `release`, `send_draft`, `update`) has an updated spec; `Destroy` has none.

**When it happens:** A future refactor of `DraftTask#attachment` or this command could silently stop destroying attachments, leaving orphaned `Attachment` records (and their uploaded files) for every deleted draft.

**Fix:** Add a case to `spec/lib/draft_tasks/commands/destroy_spec.rb` (creating it if absent) asserting the attachment record is gone after `Destroy.call`, plus a no-attachment case.

posted.title: Failure responses break the API error format
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** Failures render `{ "errors": [...] }`, but the API-wide convention is `{ "error": { code, message, details } }` (`HandlesErrors#render_error` and the 422 renderer in `Api::V1::BaseController`).

**When it happens:** A string failure like `"only the author can change the recording"` gets the new shape, while exception failures (`DraftTasks::NotEditable`) are re-raised and come back in the standard shape — two formats from one endpoint.

**Fix:** Render every failure with the existing unprocessable-entity error shape, passing `Array(error)` as the message list.

label.title: Attachment 422 body has a different shape
label.label: nit
label.note: Validation failures from ReplaceAttachment render `{ errors: [...] }` while InvalidAttachment and the rest of the API render `{ error: { code, message } }`. Status and behaviour are right; the client just has two shapes to parse.

posted.title: Shared lock error nested under one command
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `Lock::Busy` is the shared draft-lock error — raised by the `WithLockedDraft` service and rescued by the `mark_ready` and `release` commands — yet it is defined inside `Commands::SendDraft`, so a service depends on one command's namespace and sibling commands must reach into it.

**When it happens:** Renaming or refactoring `SendDraft`, or grepping for lock errors, breaks or misleads the service, two other commands, specs, and this concern.

**Fix:** Move it to a shared home, e.g. `class LockBusy < Error` in `draft_tasks/errors.rb`, and update all references.

label.title: Lock::Busy lives in the Send command but is raised by the lock service
label.label: nit
label.note: WithLockedDraft raises `DraftTasks::Commands::SendDraft::Lock::Busy`, which MarkReady and Release also rescue, so the error class is owned by one command but shared by three callers and the lock service. Behaviour is correct; this is placement.

posted.title: `count(true)` works only through accidental SQL
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `.count(true)` does not count truthy items here. On an ActiveRecord relation, Rails treats `true` as a column expression and runs `COUNT(TRUE)` SQL, which only coincidentally equals the row count.

**When it happens:** Anyone reads or edits the "caps the list" assertion and wonders what `true` means; a plain `.count` or `.length` already respects `.limit` because Rails counts limited relations via a subquery.

**Fix:** `expect(described_class.call(draft: draft).length).to eq(described_class::LIMIT)`

posted.title: Draft-claimed attachments never tested as claimed
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `claimed?` also returns true when only `draft_task_id` is set, but the new test only covers the unclaimed and task-claimed states.

**When it happens:** If `claimed?` ever loses `draft_task_id.present?`, every spec still passes while `replace_attachment` starts re-claiming uploads already owned by another draft.

**Fix:** Add the draft branch to the test:
```ruby
expect(build(:attachment, :unclaimed, draft_task_id: BSON::ObjectId.new)).to be_claimed
```

posted.title: Private-draft test never uses a list member
posted.details:
**summary:** The "hides private drafts from other list members" test requests as `create(:user)` — a user with no company or list membership. The `forbidden` therefore comes from basic access checks, not from `visibility: "private"`, so the test stays green even if private drafts are visible to every fellow list member. Remove the `draft.update!(visibility: "private")` line and it still passes, proving the visibility rule is untested.

**when:** Any regression in the private-visibility check for the new comments endpoint goes undetected by this spec.

**fix:** Request as a real other list member who is not the draft author — e.g. add a second member to `list` (or use `admin`, if admins don't bypass private visibility) instead of an ad-hoc non-member user.

posted.title: Comment list silently hides newest comments
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `chronological` sorts comments oldest-first, so `.limit(LIMIT)` keeps the oldest 50 and silently drops every newer comment.

**When it happens:** A sent task has 51 or more comments; the endpoint returns comments 1–50 and the most recent ones never appear.

**Fix:** Keep the newest 50 and reverse them for display, or use a `since` cursor like `Comments::Queries::ListComments` (which has no cap):

```ruby
Comment.where(commentable_type: "Task", commentable_id: draft.sent_task_id)
       .order(created_at: :desc).limit(LIMIT).reverse
```

posted.title: Draft lookup fires one query per comment
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** The `draft` block runs once per serialized comment, so every from-draft comment issues its own `DraftTask.find` SQL query. `find` also raises `RecordNotFound` (failing the whole response) if a referenced draft no longer exists.

**When it happens:** `CommentsController#index` renders up to 50 comments, so one request can run ~50 extra SELECTs.

**Fix:** Use a preloaded association (e.g. `comment.draft_task` with `includes`) or pass the already-loaded draft into the blueprint.

label.title: Per-comment DraftTask.find in the comments blueprint
label.label: nit
label.note: The `draft` field does `DraftTask.find(comment.draft_task_id)` per comment. The list is capped at ListDraftComments::LIMIT (50) and in practice one comment per task comes from a draft, so this is a handful of extra reads on a cold endpoint, not something to block on.

posted.title: Revision increment is not atomic
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `draft.revision + 1` reads the counter in memory and then writes a fixed number via `$set`. Two updates running at the same time both read the same value and write the same number, so one edit is never counted.

**When it happens:** The same author saves the draft from two tabs or devices at once; the `update` endpoint runs without the `WithLockedDraft` lock, so nothing serializes the two requests.

**Fix:** Increment atomically in MongoDB with `$inc` instead of computing the value in Ruby.

posted.title: Comment blueprint duplicates existing serializer fields
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `Comments::Blueprints::CommentBlueprint` already declares the same `id`, `body`, `edited_at`, `created_at`, `author_id` and `from_draft` fields for this model. This blueprint repeats all six and hand-builds the nested draft hash instead of a nested blueprint (as `attachment` does in `DraftTaskBlueprint`).

**When it happens:** Any future change to comment serialization must now be applied in two separate namespaces.

**Fix:** Reuse the existing blueprint via a Blueprinter `view` that adds the `draft` field.

posted.title: Attachment claim check races under concurrent requests
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `claimed?` is read first and the attachment is claimed later with a plain `update`, so the check and the claim are not one atomic step.

**When it happens:** The same upload id is submitted to two drafts at nearly the same time; both requests pass the check and both drafts end up claiming one attachment.

**Fix:** Claim atomically with `find_one_and_update` guarded by `draft_task_id: nil` and `task_id: nil`, mirroring how `DraftTask#claim!` guards state transitions.

posted.title: Attachment field adds N+1 queries on lists
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `draft.attachment` runs `Attachment.where(id: attachment_id).first` — one database query per draft. The new field therefore issues a query for every rendered object.

**When it happens:** Any endpoint that renders a collection of drafts (e.g. a drafts index) now fires one extra Attachment query per record, with no batching or preload possible since it is a hand-written method, not an association.

**Fix:** Batch-load the attachments (`Attachment.in(id: draft_ids)`) before rendering and resolve them from a preloaded map.

posted.title: Override test lets task points diverge from ledger
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** The test only pins the ledger amount. `SendDraft#create_task` builds the task from the draft's own `task_attributes` and never sees the `points` override, so `task.points` stays 10 while only 4 points are settled — this spec passes and hides the divergence.

**When it happens:** A sender sends a 10-point draft with `points: "4"`: the recipient sees a 10-point task, but the giver is only charged 4.

**Fix:** Also pin the task, e.g. `task = described_class.call(...).value` then `expect(task.points).to eq(4)`; if that fails, pass the override into `Tasks::Commands::Create` as well.

label.title: Ledger entry on send uses the request's points, not the reservation
label.label: real
label.note: SendDraft#settle_amount returns points.to_i when send_now carries a points param and passes it to SettleReservation, while the task is built from locked.task_attributes (the held amount) and the balance was checked against locked.points. points: 1 (or 500) moves a different amount through the ledger than was held or put on the task, with no balance check.

posted.title: No test that lock is held during block
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** No spec asserts the lock is actually held while the block runs — the core guarantee of `WithLockedGiver`. A regression that releases the lock before yielding would pass all current examples.

**When it happens:** If `call` is refactored so `lock.release` runs before `yield`, every spec stays green, but concurrent givers are no longer serialized and can double-spend points.

**Fix:** Assert inside the block that the key exists in Redis.

```ruby
  it "holds the lock while the block runs and releases it afterwards" do
    result = described_class.call(user: user, company: company) do
      expect(AppRedis.with { |redis| redis.exists?(key) }).to be(true)
      :held
    end

    expect(result).to eq(:held)
    expect(AppRedis.with { |redis| redis.exists?(key) }).to be(false)
  end
```

posted.title: Retry double-charges giver after failed send
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** The award entry is written while the draft is still `ready`, and nothing stops a second entry for the same draft. If anything fails after `write_entry` (e.g. `TaskEvent.track!` or the caller's `mark_sent!`), the draft stays `ready`, so a retry settles again.

**When it happens:** A send fails between the ledger write and the state change; the user retries and two `award` entries are created for one `draft_task_id`, charging the giver twice.

**Fix:** Make settlement idempotent — skip when an `award` entry already exists for `draft_task_id`, or enforce a unique index on it.

posted.title: Adding **options breaks existing call(title: ...) tests
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** The helper now accepts keywords via `**options`. In Ruby 3, a bare call like `call(title: "Review", ...)` sends those pairs as keywords, which `**options` swallows — the required positional `attrs` stays empty and Ruby raises `ArgumentError` (wrong number of arguments, given 0, expected 1).

**When it happens:** Running this spec file — "creates the task", "awards points", "notifies assignees" and "returns validation messages" all invoke `call(title: ...)` without braces, so four examples now error.

**Fix:** Wrap the attributes in braces at those call sites, e.g. `call({ title: "Review", assignee_ids: [member.id, admin.id] })`.

posted.title: Sent drafts ignore private visibility
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `sent_view` always shows `draft.author.display_name`, dropping the `private?` check that `pending_view` still applies. Before this change, sent drafts were never shown publicly at all, so a private draft's author was never exposed.

**When it happens:** A draft with `visibility: "private"` is marked ready and then sent; the public share page's drafts section now shows its author name. No spec covers the private + sent case.

**Fix:** Reuse the privacy rule in `sent_view`, or if showing the author after sending is intended, add a spec pinning that behavior.

label.title: Private sent drafts leak the author's name on the share page
label.label: real
label.note: DraftPublicView#call branches on draft.sent?; only pending_view consults draft.private?. sent_view always renders draft.author.display_name, and PublicList now includes drafts sent in the last 7 days, so GET /s/:token shows the author of a private draft as soon as it has a sent_task_id.

posted.title: Update query lacks the drafting-state guard
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `editable?` and the author check read the in-memory snapshot, but the write filters only on `_id`, so a draft that concurrently left `drafting` still gets edited — including `points`, after `MarkReady` already reserved the old amount against the giver's balance.

**When it happens:** The author edits the draft while it is being marked ready in another tab or by a background flow.

**Fix:** Follow the model's own `release_reservation!` pattern: query `where(_id: draft.id, state: "drafting")` and return a failure when nothing matched.

label.title: Update can overwrite a draft that was sent in the meantime
label.label: real
label.note: Update#call checks editable? on the in-memory draft, then runs DraftTask.where(_id: draft.id).find_one_and_update({"$set" => changes}) with no state filter and ignores the returned document, so an edit landing after a concurrent mark_ready + send overwrites title/points on a sent draft. It should filter on state: "drafting" and fail when nil comes back.

posted.title: Update persists changes made outside the command
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `changes` is built from `draft.changes`, which lists every unsaved change on the instance — including edits made before this command ran — so the `$set` persists those too and clobbers newer database values.

**When it happens:** The new spec "writes only the fields that changed" nils `stale.note` before calling; `draft.changes` then includes `"note" => nil`, so the `$set` overwrites the DB value and the spec's `note: "set elsewhere"` expectation is not met.

**Fix:** Diff `attrs` against a freshly loaded copy of the record and `$set` only those keys; drop the now-unused helper.

posted.title: Unvalidated points param bypasses giving budget
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `send_now` passes raw `params[:points]` into the settle amount with no server-side bound. Budget checks only ran on the draft's reserved `points` field, so the settled amount is never validated anywhere.

**When it happens:** `POST /api/v1/draft_tasks/1/send_now?points=1000000` on a draft that reserved 50 points writes a 1,000,000-point award entry.

**Fix:** Clamp or reject the override in `settle_amount`, e.g. `requested.clamp(0, locked.points)`.

label.title: Ledger entry on send uses the request's points, not the reservation
label.label: real
label.note: SendDraft#settle_amount returns points.to_i when send_now carries a points param and passes it to SettleReservation, while the task is built from locked.task_attributes (the held amount) and the balance was checked against locked.points. points: 1 (or 500) moves a different amount through the ledger than was held or put on the task, with no balance check.

posted.title: Giver lock doesn't serialize other balance writers
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** The new giver lock is only acquired by `mark_ready`. Commands that mutate the same totals — `send_draft` (settles a reservation into spent points), `release`, and `update` — never take it, so the balance check followed by `mark_ready!` is still not atomic.

**When it happens:** A user marks draft A ready while sending ready draft D. `GivingBalance` reads `spent` and `reserved` in two separate queries; D's settlement commits between them, inflating `remaining` by D's points, so A is approved beyond budget.

**Fix:** Have every writer of spent/reserved points acquire the same giver lock (in `settle_reservation`, `release`, `update`), or enforce the cap with one atomic DB query/transaction.

posted.title: Spec never asserts the debited user
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** The award entry's `user_id` — the giver whose balance is debited — is never asserted. The `task` fixture is also created with `author: member`, the same user as the draft author, so giver and task author are indistinguishable here.

**When it happens:** If `write_entry` debited `task.author` or any other user instead of `draft.author`, all six examples still pass, silently corrupting the giving ledger.

**Fix:** Assert the user and give the task a different author:

```ruby
expect(result.value).to have_attributes(
  amount: 10, kind: "award", user_id: draft.author.id,
  task_id: task.id, draft_task_id: draft.id, note: PointsLedgerEntry::ESCROW_NOTE
)
```

posted.title: No-op spec can't detect an unwanted write
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** The draft is created moments before the call, so `updated_at` is always within 1 second of `created_at`. The assertion passes even if the command does save, so it never actually proves the no-op.

**When it happens:** If `Update` starts bumping `updated_at` on unchanged input, this spec stays green and the regression ships unnoticed.

**Fix:** Compare with the pre-call value instead:

```ruby
updated_before = draft.updated_at
expect(draft.reload.updated_at).to eq(updated_before)
```

posted.title: Budget validation blocks unrelated edits and sends
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `points_within_budget` runs on every save, not only when `points` changes. Once a draft's points exceed the current budget, the record cannot be saved at all, even for unrelated changes.

**When it happens:** An author has a draft with 30 points; an admin lowers the weekly budget to 20. The author then fixes a title typo and the save fails with "Points exceeds your weekly budget of 20". The `update!` inside `mark_sent` fails the same way, turning a send into a validation exception instead of a graceful failure.

**Fix:** Only validate when points actually change: `validate :points_within_budget, if: -> { new_record? || points_changed? }` (the real remaining-balance check stays in `MarkReady`/`GivingBalance`).

posted.title: author_name field adds N+1 queries on lists
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** The new `draft.author.display_name` lookup loads the author `User` lazily, once per rendered draft. List endpoints now fire one extra query per draft.

**When it happens:** `GET /api/v1/draft_tasks` or `/reservations` with 100 drafts triggers up to 100 extra `User` loads, even when all drafts share the same author.

**Fix:** Eager load the association in the queries, e.g. add `.includes(:author)` to `ListDrafts` and `ListReservations`.

label.label: nit

posted.title: Escrow total stays wrong after Send now
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** The `sendNow` patch keeps the draft's old `reserved_points`, but the server computes `reserved_points` as `ready? ? points : 0`, so a sent draft holds 0. The "points held in escrow" header keeps counting points that were already settled.

**When it happens:** A ready draft holding 5 points is sent; the header still shows those 5 points as held until the page is reloaded (the effect only refetches when `listId` changes).

**Fix:** Mirror the server value in the local patch.

```tsx
{ ...item, state: "sent", sent_task_id: task.id, reserved_points: 0 }
```

posted.title: Adding **options breaks existing keyword-style spec calls
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** In Ruby 3, once `call` accepts keywords (`**options`), bare keywords are no longer packed into the positional `attrs` hash; they all go into `options`, leaving the required `attrs` empty. `call(title: "x")` now raises `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (given 0, expected 1)`.

**When it happens:** Running this spec file: the "creates the task", "awards points", "notifies assignees" and "returns validation messages" examples all fail with that error.

**Fix:** Wrap attrs in braces at those call sites, e.g. `call({ title: "Review", assignee_ids: [member.id, admin.id] })`.

posted.title: Update writes every dirty field, not just attrs
posted.details:
**what_is_wrong:** The `$set` is built from `draft.changes`, which holds *all* pending in-memory changes on the draft object, not only the `attrs` passed to the command. So unrelated dirty fields get force-written, silently clobbering database values.

**when_it_happens:** The new spec "writes only the fields that changed" sets `stale.note = nil` before updating `title`; `note => nil` is included in the `$set`, so the `note: "set elsewhere"` expectation fails and the suite goes red.

**fix:** Restrict the write to the command's own fields: `draft.changes.slice(*attrs.keys.map(&:to_s)).transform_values(&:last)`.

posted.title: Sent private drafts expose the author name
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `pending_view` hides the author when `draft.private?`, but `sent_view` always returns `draft.author.display_name`, so a private draft loses its anonymity as soon as it is sent.

**When it happens:** A draft with `visibility: "private"` gets sent; the public share page then shows the author's display name. No spec covers the private + sent case.

**Fix:** Unless the linked task already reveals the author publicly on purpose, mirror the guard:

```ruby
author_name: draft.private? ? nil : draft.author.display_name,
```

label.title: Private sent drafts leak the author's name on the share page
label.label: real
label.note: DraftPublicView#call branches on draft.sent?; only pending_view consults draft.private?. sent_view always renders draft.author.display_name, and PublicList now includes drafts sent in the last 7 days, so GET /s/:token shows the author of a private draft as soon as it has a sent_task_id.

posted.title: Retry after partial failure double-awards points
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** The settle is not idempotent. The ledger entry is saved while the draft is still `ready`, and nothing stops a second entry for the same draft — the `draft_task_id` index is not unique and the command has no existing-entry check.

**When it happens:** If `TaskEvent.track!` or the caller's later `mark_sent!` raises, the draft stays `ready` with the award already persisted; the user retries the send and a second `award` entry is created, double-spending the escrowed points.

**Fix:** Return the existing entry when one is already recorded, and/or make the `draft_task_id` index unique so `create!` fails on duplicates.

posted.title: Escrowed path lets send_now award unlimited points
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** With `escrowed: true` the balance check is skipped entirely, but the only caller (`DraftTasks::Commands::SendDraft`) settles a user-supplied amount that is never validated against the reservation or the author's budget.

**When it happens:** `POST /api/v1/draft_tasks/:id/send_now` with `points=1000000` on a draft that reserved 10 points: the task is created unchecked, then `Points::Commands::SettleReservation` awards 1,000,000 points (the task's own `points` and the ledger amount even diverge).

**Fix:** Validate the override in `SendDraft#settle_amount` — reject `points` above `locked.points`, or re-check `GivingBalance` for the excess before settling.

posted.title: Suspended-company exclusion is never actually verified
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** The first example creates a `:suspended` company, but that company has no draft tasks, so `DraftTask.ready.count eq 0` passes even if the job wrongly processes suspended companies.

**When it happens:** If `Company.active` in `perform` regresses to `Company.all`, reservations in suspended companies get released and this spec still stays green.

**Fix:** Give the suspended company a stale reservation and assert it survives:

```ruby
frozen = create(:draft_task, :ready, company: suspended, author: create(:user), points: 5)
expect(frozen.reload).to be_ready
```

posted.title: No-op test cannot detect a forced write
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `be_within(1.second)` is too loose: an accidental write happens milliseconds after creation, so `updated_at` still sits within a second of `created_at`. The example passes even when the no-op guard is broken, so it guards nothing.

**When it happens:** If the `changes.empty?` early return in `Update` is removed, every update writes `updated_at`, yet this spec stays green.

**Fix:** Create the draft first, then travel time forward so a forced write moves `updated_at` measurably (needs `ActiveSupport::Testing::TimeHelpers`): wrap the call and assertion in `travel_to(draft.created_at + 1.hour)`.

posted.title: Failed settlement leaves orphaned task behind
posted.details:
**summary:** The task is persisted (with its `task.created` webhook and assignee notifications) before settlement runs. If `SettleReservation` then fails, `finalize` just returns the failure: the saved task is left orphaned, because `WithLockedDraft` is only a Redis lock with no rollback. The draft stays `ready`, so a retry creates a duplicate task.

**when:** `SettleReservation` returns a failure or raises (e.g. the draft is no longer `ready`, or `PointsLedgerEntry.create!` hits a DB/validation error) after the task is already saved.

**fix:** Compensate on failure by destroying the just-created task before returning, or wrap task creation + settlement + `mark_sent!` in one DB transaction.

posted.title: Ready-to-drafting transition now has two implementations
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** The command now uses the atomic `release_reservation!`, but the old AASM event `resume_drafting` (DraftTask) still performs the same ready-to-drafting transition non-atomically. No app code calls `resume_drafting!` anymore; only its model spec keeps it alive.

**When it happens:** A future caller picks `draft.resume_drafting!` and reintroduces the race `release_reservation!` was built to prevent (e.g., concurrent stale-reservation release), or the two paths drift in what they clear.

**Fix:** Remove the `resume_drafting` event and its spec test, or make it delegate to `release_reservation!`.

posted.title: Escrow total stays wrong after Send now
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `sendNow` builds the updated row locally instead of using the server's draft, so the old `reserved_points` is kept. The backend settles the reservation on send (`Points::Commands::SettleReservation` in `SendDraft`), so a reloaded draft would show `reserved_points: 0`. This also diverges from `transition`, which trusts the server response.

**When it happens:** Click "Send now" on a ready draft; the row flips to "Sent" but "{held} points held in escrow" still counts that draft's points until the page is reloaded.

**Fix:** Have `send_now` return the updated `DraftTask` like `mark_ready` does, or zero it locally:

```
{ ...item, state: "sent", sent_task_id: task.id, reserved_points: 0 }
```

posted.title: Replies pagination cursor discarded, threads truncated
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** Slack's `conversations.replies` is paginated, but only the first page is kept — `next_cursor` is thrown away. Unlike `messages` and `channels`, this method returns a raw array instead of `Connectors::Page`.

**When it happens:** A thread with more replies than `limit` (the caller `ListMessages` passes 500) silently loses the overflow; those replies are never synced or indexed.

**Fix:** Return a `Connectors::Page` so the caller can follow the cursor until it's empty.

label.title: Thread replies are capped at 500 and never paged
label.label: nit
label.note: replies_for fetches conversations.replies once with limit REPLY_LIMIT (500) and no oldest, then filters by since client-side; a thread with more than 500 replies silently loses the rest and the window is only applied to what came back. Needs a 500-reply thread inside a 14-day window to matter.

posted.title: New replies to old threads are never synced
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** Replies are only fetched for parents returned by `conversations.history` with `oldest: since`. Slack filters parents by their own timestamp, so a thread started before the window never appears and its newer replies are skipped entirely.

**When it happens:** A thread started 20 days ago (past the 14-day default window) gets a reply today; that reply is never indexed.

**Fix:** Slack has no "threads with recent activity" query; document the gap, or scan parents without `oldest` and expand only threads whose `latest_reply` falls inside the window.

posted.title: Multi-page test never asserts collected items
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** The new page-budget test checks `pages_fetched` and `next_cursor` but never inspects `result.items`, even though its stub builds a distinct node per page. So aggregation of items across pages is untested for this query.

**When it happens:** If `items.concat(page.items)` in the query regressed to keeping only the last page, every example in this file would still pass.

**Fix:** Assert the accumulated items the stub already produces:

```ruby
expect(result.items.map { |item| item[:external_id] }).to eq(%w[lin-ENG-1 lin-ENG-2 lin-ENG-3])
```

posted.title: Repeated providers duplicate search results and API calls
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `Registry.for` never removes duplicate entries from the provider list, so the same tool is returned twice.

**When it happens:** A request like `?providers[]=github&providers[]=github` resolves to the GitHub tool twice; `ConnectedSearch` then runs it twice, duplicating items in the response and doubling calls to the external API.

**Fix:**
```ruby
wanted.uniq.map { |provider| find(provider) }
```

posted.title: Invalid `kind` silently falls back to issues search
posted.details:
**summary:** Any `kind` value other than exactly `"pull_request"` silently runs the issues query instead of erroring. The declared enum is never enforced at runtime, unlike `pages` (validated in `Base#call`) and Slack's `channel` (raises `Connectors::InvalidInput`), so an explicitly wrong value is treated as the documented default.

**when:** The tool caller (LLM) sends `kind: "pr"`, `"issues"` or `"pull requests"`; the user silently gets issue results when they asked for pull requests, with no error to signal the mismatch.

**fix:** Keep the blank-means-issue default, but raise for values outside `KINDS`, mirroring the `Connectors::InvalidInput` pattern used for Slack's `channel` param.

posted.title: Thread fetching multiplies Slack API calls
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** Every parent with replies triggers an extra `conversations.replies` call, and each reply then goes through `normalize`, which calls `chat.getPermalink` — one HTTP request per reply. Hitting Slack's rate limit raises `Connectors::RateLimited` and aborts the whole query.

**When it happens:** One page with 50 threaded messages averaging 20 replies ≈ 1,100 API calls.

**Fix:** Build permalinks locally (`https://<team>.slack.com/archives/<channel>/p<ts>`) instead of one `chat.getPermalink` request per item.

posted.title: Pages validation uses hardcoded cap, not configured one
posted.details:
**summary:** The `pages` input is validated against the hardcoded `PageLimit::MAX_PAGES` (5), but the fallback default uses the configurable `PageLimit.max_pages` (`config.x.connectors.max_pages_per_call`).

**when:** If an operator raises the config to 10, `pages: 8` is wrongly rejected even though the default allows 10. If they lower it to 3, `pages: 5` is accepted and fetches 5 pages, bypassing the operator's cap.

**fix:** Validate against the effective limit so both directions stay consistent:
```ruby
optional(:pages).maybe(:integer, gt?: 0, lteq?: Connectors::Services::PageLimit.max_pages)
```

posted.title: Pagination off-by-one fetches an empty extra page
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `page_number * per_page <= total_count` returns a next-page cursor even when every matching result has already been fetched, so one extra request is made for a page that is guaranteed empty.

**When it happens:** A user has 100 matching pull requests with `per_page: 50`; after fetching page 2, `2 * 50 <= 100` yields a cursor for page 3, which returns zero items (and burns one of the `PageLimit` page slots).

**Fix:** Use strict less-than:

```
next_page = page_number * per_page < body.fetch("total_count", 0) ? page_number + 1 : nil
```

label.title: Exact multiple of per_page triggers one extra empty search call
label.label: nit
label.note: pull_requests computes next_page with page_number * per_page <= total_count, so when total_count is exactly 50 or 100 the walk requests one more page that returns zero items before stopping. One wasted request in a rare case; should be <.

posted.title: Page limit validated against constant, not configured max
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** The schema caps `pages` with the hardcoded `PageLimit::MAX_PAGES` (5), but the real budget is `PageLimit.max_pages`, which reads the `max_pages_per_call` config. Two sources of truth for the same limit, even within this file.

**When it happens:** With `max_pages_per_call = 2`, a caller passing `pages: 5` passes validation and fetches 5 pages, bypassing the configured cap; with `= 10`, valid values 6–10 are rejected.

**Fix:** Use one source, e.g. clamp the input: `[input[:pages] || PageLimit.max_pages, PageLimit.max_pages].min`.
