posted.title: Connected search endpoint 500s on every request
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `ConnectedSearch` accepts a `cursors:` hash and exposes `next_cursors`; the action passes `cursor:` (unknown keyword → `ArgumentError`) and reads `result.next_cursor` (undefined → `NoMethodError`).

**When it happens:** Every `GET /api/v1/search/connected` call crashes and `HandlesErrors` returns a 500; the new request specs (sending `cursors[github]=2`, expecting `next_cursors`) fail.

**Fix:** Pass `cursors: params[:cursors]` and render `next_cursors: result.next_cursors`.

posted.title: Spec uses wrong cursor API; tests fail
posted.details:
**summary:** **What's wrong:** The spec calls `ConnectedSearch.call` with `cursor:` (singular string) and reads `result.next_cursor`, but the query only accepts `cursors:` (a per-provider hash, as the controller passes) and its `Result` struct exposes `next_cursors`, not `next_cursor`. Both example assertions can never pass.

**When it happens:** Running this spec: `described_class.call(..., cursor: "abc")` raises `ArgumentError: unknown keyword :cursor` before any tool stub is hit; even if fixed, `result.next_cursor` raises `NoMethodError` on the struct.

**Fix:** Pass the per-provider cursors hash and assert the returned hash:

**fix:** ```ruby
result = described_class.call(company: company, user: member, q: "x",
  cursors: { "github" => "abc", "slack" => "abc" })
...
expect(result.next_cursors).to eq("github" => "2", "slack" => "dXNlcjpV")
```

posted.title: Pagination keeps only the last provider's cursor
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** When several connected providers each return a `next_cursor`, only the last one is kept and the others are dropped. That single cursor is then broadcast to every tool as if it were its own pagination token.

**When it happens:** GitHub and Slack are both truncated: the next request feeds Slack's cursor into the GitHub query, which starts paging from it (see `ListIssues#call`), giving wrong or duplicate items.

**Fix:** Build a per-provider cursor map (e.g. JSON) and have each tool read its own entry.

label.title: One cursor is reused across providers, so Slack's cursor is sent to GitHub
label.label: real
label.note: early ConnectedSearch takes a single cursor and passes it to every tool in Registry.for(providers); next_cursor is whichever provider's came last, so the second page of a multi-provider search sends Slack's opaque cursor to GitHub's page-number query (to_i => 0 => page 1 again) and vice versa. Head keys cursors by provider (cursors[tool.provider], next_cursors hash). Fixed at head.

posted.title: Capped syncs skip items after cursor wipe
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `touch_synced!` now always clears `cursor`, and `SyncAccountJob` discards each query's `next_cursor` while `PageLimit` caps runs at 5 pages. A capped run still advances `last_synced_at`, so items past page 5 can fall outside the next lookback window and never be imported.

**When it happens:** A busy Slack channel posts more than 5 pages of messages since `since`; the run stops early, the sync is marked done, and the excess messages age out of the window.

**Fix:** Persist `result.next_cursor` (restore a `cursor:` param) or don't advance `last_synced_at` when `PageLimit.capped?(pages_fetched)`.

label.title: Sync advances last_synced_at even when the page cap cut the walk short
label.label: real
label.note: perform discards result.next_cursor and calls account.touch_synced!(synced_at: started_at) (early: touch_synced!) regardless of whether pages_fetched hit PageLimit.max_pages; the next run's LookBack starts at last_synced_at - 5 minutes, so items older than the last fetched page but newer than the previous watermark are never imported. Any account with more than 5 pages (250 GitHub issues, 500 Slack messages) in a window silently loses the rest. Real: data loss on the sync path every run.

posted.title: Expected `since` never matches LookBack's output
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `expected_since` is midnight on 2026-10-02, but `LookBack` only ever returns `last_synced_at - 5.minutes` or `now - 14.days` (09:00) — never a beginning-of-day value. The shared context also sets `last_synced_at: 2.days.ago`, so the 14-day floor branch is not even taken.

**When it happens:** Running this example: the job passes `since: last_synced_at - OVERLAP`, so both `have_received(...).with(since: expected_since)` assertions fail and the example is red.

**Fix:** Force the window branch and expect the exact floor:
```ruby
account.update!(last_synced_at: nil)
expected_since = Time.zone.parse("2026-10-16 09:00:00") - Connectors::Services::LookBack::DEFAULT_WINDOW
```

posted.title: Never-ending stub cursor duplicates fetched messages
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** The `messages` stub always returns the same page with `next_cursor: "abc"`, so `ListMessages` keeps paginating until the page cap and appends the same messages on every round.

**When it happens:** Running this example: the result holds `"deploy done"` once per fetched page, so `eq(["deploy done"])` fails (or the loop hangs if unbounded).

**Fix:** Cap the fetch to a single page, e.g. `described_class.call(company: company, user: member, channel: "C456", q: "deploy", pages: 1)`.

posted.title: New client pagination logic has no tests
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** The new cursor logic has no test coverage. Every spec stubs `Connectors::Github::Client` with fabricated `Connectors::Page` objects, and no client spec exists.

**When it happens:** The `<=` off-by-one ships green today; any future change to `total_count` or `Link`-header handling is likewise unverified.

**Fix:** Add a `Connectors::Github::Client` spec with stubbed HTTP responses covering full page, exact multiple of `per_page`, last page, and empty result.

posted.title: API errors silently become empty PR pages
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `get` only raises on 401 and 429. Other errors (GitHub uses 403 for secondary rate limits) return a JSON error object, and `body.fetch("items", [])` turns it into an empty page that looks like success.

**When it happens:** GitHub answers 403 with `{"message": "...rate limit..."}` during a PR sync; the loop sees no items and no cursor, ends quietly, and the run reports zero pull requests.

**Fix:** Raise on any non-2xx status in `get`, or treat a body missing `"items"`/`"total_count"` as an error.

posted.title: Request cursor param never reaches the endpoint
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** The endpoint reads cursors from `params[:cursors]` (a provider-keyed hash in `cursor_params`), but the spec sends a top-level `cursor` param, which is ignored.

**When it happens:** The client stub requires `cursor: "2"`, yet `ConnectedSearch` passes `cursor: nil` from the empty cursors hash, so RSpec raises an unexpected-arguments error and the example fails.

**Fix:** Send the param the endpoint accepts:

```ruby
params: { q: "flaky", providers: ["github"], cursors: { github: "2" }, since_days: "3" }
```

posted.title: Spec asserts next_cursor key endpoint never returns
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** The endpoint renders `next_cursors`, a per-provider hash like `{"github" => 3}`, not a `next_cursor` string. `json["next_cursor"]` is always nil.

**When it happens:** In this example, so `expect(json["next_cursor"]).to eq("3")` fails even when the request succeeds.

**Fix:** Assert the real shape: `expect(json["next_cursors"]).to eq("github" => 3)` — the stub builds an integer `next_cursor: 3`, and nothing converts it to a string.

posted.title: README pagination params don't match the endpoint
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** The HTTP endpoint does not use `cursor`/`next_cursor`. Its response is `next_cursors`, a hash keyed by provider, and it accepts `cursors[<provider>]` on the next request (see `SearchController#cursor_params`).

**When it happens:** A client follows the README and calls `?q=bug&cursor=abc`; the param is silently ignored, so every call returns the first page again.

**Fix:** Document the real contract: "returns further pages via `next_cursors`; pass each back as `cursors[<provider>]`".

posted.title: Duplicate providers run the same search twice
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `Registry.for` maps each requested provider without removing duplicates, so the same tool can be returned and executed more than once.

**When it happens:** A request like `?providers[]=github&providers[]=github` runs `GithubSearch` twice, doubling external API calls and likely returning every GitHub item twice.

**Fix:** Deduplicate the list before resolving tools:

```ruby
wanted = Array(providers).map(&:to_s).reject(&:blank?).uniq
```

posted.title: Pages validation ignores configured page cap
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `pages` is validated against the hard-coded `PageLimit::MAX_PAGES` (5), but the fallback in `max_pages` uses the configurable `PageLimit.max_pages`, so the two limits disagree.

**When it happens:** With `max_pages_per_call` configured to 10, `pages: 8` raises `InvalidInput` even though a run without `pages` fetches 10 pages; configured to 3, callers can still force 5.

**Fix:** Validate against `Connectors::Services::PageLimit.max_pages` so input validation and the fallback share one source of truth.

posted.title: Thread replies add unbounded N+1 API calls
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** Every thread parent adds one `conversations.replies` HTTP call, and every reply then adds a `chat.getPermalink` call inside `normalize`. None of these count toward the page budget, so a single page can fire hundreds of sequential calls.

**When it happens:** A page of 100 messages where 40 have threads produces ~180 calls; Slack returns 429, `Connectors::RateLimited` is raised, and the whole sync aborts.

**Fix:** Skip threads whose `latest_reply` is older than `since`, and build permalinks locally from channel and `ts` instead of one API call per message.

posted.title: Replies of subtyped parents are never fetched
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** Replies are only fetched for parents that survive the subtype filter, so threads started by `file_share` or `bot_message` messages lose all of their replies.

**When it happens:** A file share starts a thread with ten human replies; none of them end up in the indexed items.

**Fix:** Gate only the parent's normalization, not the reply fetch:
```ruby
page.items.each do |raw|
  items << normalize(raw) unless raw["subtype"]
  items.concat(replies_for(raw, since)) if raw["reply_count"].to_i.positive?
end
```

posted.title: Thread replies beyond one page are silently dropped
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** Slack's `conversations.replies` paginates like `conversations.history`, but this method discards `response_metadata.next_cursor`, so only the first page of a thread is returned.

**When it happens:** A thread with more than 500 replies (the caller's `REPLY_LIMIT` in `ListMessages`); replies after the first 500 never sync and are silently missing from search.

**Fix:** Return `Connectors::Page` and pass the cursor, mirroring `messages` (update `replies_for` to follow it):

```ruby
def replies(channel:, ts:, cursor: nil, limit: LIMIT)
  body = post("conversations.replies", channel: channel, ts: ts, cursor: cursor, limit: limit)
  Connectors::Page.new(items: body.fetch("messages", []), next_cursor: next_cursor(body))
end
```

label.label: nit
label.note: replies_for fetches conversations.replies once with limit REPLY_LIMIT (500) and no oldest, then filters by since client-side; a thread with more than 500 replies silently loses the rest and the window is only applied to what came back. Needs a 500-reply thread inside a 14-day window to matter.

posted.title: Connector routes dropped, spec claims "every route"
posted.details:
**what_is_wrong:** The real router stores the `/connectors` routes in a `connectorRoutes` array, attached via an entry with no `path` and `children: connectorRoutes`. `RouteParser#entry` returns early when `path` is missing, so those three routes are silently dropped from discovery, yet the spec titled "parses every route" never checks them.

**when_it_happens:** Running `described_class.call` against the real router: `/connectors`, `/connectors/:id`, and `/connectors/:id/items` are absent from the result, but every assertion in this spec still passes.

**fix:** Add `"/connectors"` to the `include` assertion — it fails today — then fix `RouteParser` so an entry without `path` still yields its `children` (and ideally follows array references like `connectorRoutes`).

label.title: Route groups the parser cannot read are silently dropped, so their pages are pruned as stale
label.label: real
label.note: RouteParser#entry returns [] for an object with no `path` without descending, and entries finds no `{` after `children: connectorRoutes` (an identifier, not an array literal), so the three /connectors routes never reach the upsert and prune deletes them on the first reindex; same for a capitalised `Component` key. Unreadable shapes must be marked or fail the reindex, never pruned.

posted.title: Failed /me fetch leaves page loading forever
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `get("/me")` throws an `ApiError` on any non-2xx response and rejects on network errors, but the promise has no `.catch`. `allowed` stays `null`, so users see "Loading..." forever, plus an unhandled rejection in the console.

**When it happens:** The stored API key expires and `GET /api/v1/me` returns 401; every admin page hangs on "Loading..." with no error or way forward.

**Fix:** Handle the rejection:

```tsx
get<Profile>("/me")
  .then((profile) => setAllowed(roleFor(profile) === "staff"))
  .catch(() => setAllowed(false));
```

posted.title: New SourceMask service has no specs
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `SourceMask` is a new hand-written tokenizer with tricky escape and template-literal logic, but the PR adds no spec for it, while sibling `ConstantResolver` got one.

**When it happens:** Any change to `mask_string`/`mask_template` (e.g., the escape gap above) passes CI, because `discover_routes_spec` never exercises strings containing quotes, braces, commas, or backticks.

**Fix:** Add `spec/lib/search/services/source_mask_spec.rb` covering quoted strings, escapes, nested templates, and unterminated input.

posted.title: Role permission lists duplicated from permissions.ts
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** The `MEMBER`/`ADMIN`/`STAFF` constants hand-copy the role-to-permission lists that already exist in `app/javascript/permissions.ts` (`ROLE_PERMISSIONS`). The two copies can drift apart silently.

**When it happens:** A new permission like `reports:read` is added to `permissions.ts` and gates a route; the Ruby lists never include it, so search hides that route for every role while the app itself still shows it.

**Fix:** Treat `permissions.ts` as the single source of truth: resolve the role lists via `ConstantResolver` at index time (store allowed roles on `RouteIndexEntry`), or add a spec that parses `permissions.ts` and asserts these constants match.

posted.title: No test for unreadable entries becoming readable
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** The command's headline change is marking entries `unreadable: true` instead of deleting them, with `upsert` resetting `unreadable` to `false`. No spec covers that reset: the `unreadable: false` assertion in the first test runs on a brand-new record where the default is already `false`, so it cannot catch a regression.

**When it happens:** A route fails to parse once (entry marked unreadable), then parses fine again; if a refactor of `upsert` drops the `unreadable: false` reset, every existing spec still passes and the route stays hidden from search forever.

**Fix:** Add a test that re-indexes an unreadable entry with a readable route and asserts the flag flips back (the unused `:unreadable` factory trait exists for this):

```ruby
it "clears unreadable when a route becomes readable again" do
  existing = create(:route_index_entry, :unreadable, path: "/a")

  described_class.call(routes: [route("/a")], now: now)

  expect(existing.reload).to have_attributes(unreadable: false, indexed_at: now)
end
```

label.title: No spec covers a flag change on a route whose permission is unchanged
label.label: nit
label.note: the "updates existing entries" example only changes permission old->new; UpsertRouteIndex#upsert does write flag, so this is a missing assertion, not a bug.

posted.title: Escaped backticks end template masking early
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `mask_template` ignores backslash escapes, while `mask_string` handles them. In JavaScript, `\`` inside a template literal is an escaped backtick, not the end of the literal.

**When it happens:** A router file containing `He said \`hi\`` inside a template stops masking at the first escaped backtick; the rest is treated as code, corrupting `RouteParser`'s brace counting (wrong routes or `Search::ParseError`).

**Fix:** Skip escape sequences at the top of the loop, as `mask_string` does.

posted.title: Component regex misses `.then()`-wrapped imports
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `LAZY` requires the `import("")` call to be the entire component value. An import followed by `.then(...)` doesn't match, so `component_at` returns `nil`.

**When it happens:** The `admin.index` route in `app-router.tsx` uses `import("./pages/AdminRoutesPage").then((m) => ...)`, so it fails `Route#readable?` and is lost from the route index.

**Fix:** Capture the module path and ignore anything after the import call.

posted.title: Stale tsconfig alias crashes with raw Errno::ENOENT
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** The alias branch of `resolve` skips the `File.exist?` check that the relative branch performs, so `constant_value`'s `File.read` raises a raw `Errno::ENOENT` instead of the intended `Search::UnresolvedConstant`.

**When it happens:** Any `compilerOptions.paths` entry whose target file is missing — for example an alias written without the `.ts` extension (the usual TypeScript style) or a module that was moved or renamed.

**Fix:** Mirror the relative branch: try the target with and without extensions, and return nil unless a candidate exists so callers get `Search::UnresolvedConstant`.

posted.title: Reindex errors silent; duplicate clicks allowed
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `reindex` is an async click handler with no `catch`, so a failed POST rejects unhandled and the UI shows nothing. The button also stays enabled, so extra clicks start concurrent reindex requests.

**When it happens:** Admin double-clicks "Reindex", or the POST fails while the server indexes routes.

**Fix:** Catch errors into an error message and disable the button while a reindex runs.

posted.title: Failed load leaves page stuck on Loading
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `get` throws `ApiError` on any failed response, but this fetch has no `catch`. The page then stays on "Loading..." forever with no error message.

**When it happens:** The admin opens the page with an expired API key (401) or the endpoint returns a 500.

**Fix:** Add error state, chain a `.catch` onto the fetch, and render the message instead of the loading text.

posted.title: New flagEnabled helper has no callers
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `flagEnabled` is exported but nothing in the codebase calls it, so no client-side flag check actually runs through it.

**When it happens:** Searching the repo at this commit, the only mention of `flagEnabled` is its own definition; the router and pages never invoke it.

**Fix:** Wire it into route matching (e.g., filter routes in `findRoute`) or remove it until a caller exists.

posted.title: Missing-router test expects [] but code raises
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** The example expects `described_class.call(router_path: "/nowhere/app-router.tsx")` to return `[]`, but `DiscoverRoutes#read_source` rescues `Errno::ENOENT` and raises `Search::RouterMissing`, so this example can never pass.

**When it happens:** On every test run — the path does not exist, so the query raises instead of returning.

**Fix:** Pick one behavior: assert the raise, or make `read_source` return `[]` and delete `RouterMissing`.

posted.title: Apostrophe in comment corrupts route masking
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** The scanner never skips comments, so a `'` inside a comment opens a string mask that runs to the next apostrophe or end of file, replacing real code with `#`.

**When it happens:** Add `// Don't edit manually` above `export const routes` in `app-router.tsx`; the masked text hides that line, `ROUTES_ARRAY` fails to match, and all routes silently vanish from the index.

**Fix:** Skip `//` and `/* */` comment regions (and regex literals) in `call` before testing `QUOTES`.

label.title: A comment between entries that contains a bracket makes parsing raise
label.label: nit
label.note: SourceMask does not mask // or /* */ comments, so a `{` or `[` inside a comment between two entries unbalances closing_index and raises Search::ParseError; app-router.tsx has no comments.

posted.title: Named-export lazy imports lose their component
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `LAZY` requires closing parens immediately after `import("...")`, so the named-export form `.then((m) => ({ default: m.X }))` fails to match and `component_at` returns `nil`.

**When it happens:** The `admin.index` route in `app-router.tsx` imports `AdminRoutesPage` with exactly that `.then` form, so it is indexed without a component and fails `Route#readable?`.

**Fix:** Allow trailing content after the import call, e.g. `LAZY = /\A(?:requireAdmin\()?\s*lazy\(\(\)\s*=>\s*import\("(?<module>[^"]*)"\).*\z/`.

posted.title: Path-less route wrappers silently drop all children
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `entry` returns `[]` before it ever parses `children` when a wrapper route has no `path` of its own, and constant references like `children: connectorRoutes` are never expanded because only literal text is scanned.

**When it happens:** `app-router.tsx` groups the connector pages as `{ flag: FLAGS.CONNECTORS, children: connectorRoutes }`, so `/connectors`, `/connectors/:id` and `/connectors/:id/items` (all gated by `PERMISSIONS.CONNECTORS_READ`) silently vanish from the route index.

**Fix:** Parse `children` before the early return, and expand constant `children` references through the resolver.

posted.title: Role permission sets duplicated in Ruby and TypeScript
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** The role→permission mapping (`MEMBER`/`ADMIN`/`STAFF`) is defined both here and in `app/javascript/permissions.ts`, and `"admin:staff"` is already defined as `Search::Services::RouteParser::ADMIN_PERMISSION`. Two sources of truth for authorization data.

**When it happens:** A gated route is added to the router with a new permission token; this Ruby list isn't updated, so `SearchRoutes` silently hides that route from every role.

**Fix:** Reuse `RouteParser::ADMIN_PERMISSION` here and add a spec asserting parity with the sets in `permissions.ts`.

posted.title: requireAdmin wrapper breaks component type contract
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `RouteDefinition.component` is typed as `LazyExoticComponent`, but `requireAdmin()` returns a plain `ComponentType`, so the two admin route entries fail TypeScript checking.

**When it happens:** Any `tsc` type-check run (this PR adds `tsconfig.json`) errors on the `admin.companies` and `admin.company` definitions.

**Fix:** Widen the field: `component?: LazyExoticComponent<ComponentType<unknown>> | ComponentType<unknown>;`

posted.title: Failed /me request leaves page loading forever
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `get("/me")` throws on any failed request, but the promise has no `.catch()`. `allowed` stays `null`, so the page shows "Loading..." forever and logs an unhandled rejection.

**When it happens:** someone opens `/admin/companies` without a valid API key; `/me` returns 401 and the spinner never ends.

**Fix:** Add `.catch(() => setAllowed(false))` (or a distinct error state) so every request outcome resolves the gate.

posted.title: Filter test can't distinguish name from path
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `q: "task"` matches both the name (`tasks.index`) and the path (`/tasks`), so this test stays green even if either branch of the query's name/path `$or` matcher is removed or broken.

**When it happens:** A regression that drops path-only or name-only matching in `SearchRoutes#call` — CI still passes because the other field still matches.

**Fix:** Add cases that match only one field, plus a no-hit case:
```ruby
expect(search(member, q: "/tasks")).to eq([tasks]) # path only
expect(search(member, q: "index")).to eq([tasks])  # name only
expect(search(member, q: "nomatch")).to be_empty
```

posted.title: New flagEnabled helper has no callers
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** `flagEnabled` is exported but nothing in the repository calls it. Routes already declare `flag` values (`FLAGS.POINTS_LEDGER`, `FLAGS.CONNECTORS`), yet no client-side code ever checks them, so the helper ships as dead code.

**When it happens:** Grep for `flagEnabled` across the repo matches only its definition in this file; the flagged routes stay reachable because nothing filters on `flag`.

**Fix:** Either wire `flagEnabled` into the route resolution/filtering logic, or remove the unused export if gating is handled server-side only.

posted.title: Failed API calls leave page stuck loading
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** No request has error handling. A failed initial load leaves `index` as `null`, so the page shows "Loading..." forever; a failed `reindex` is silently swallowed.

**When it happens:** The admin's token expires and `GET /admin/route_index` returns 401 — `ApiError` is thrown with no `catch`, so the page never renders data.

**Fix:** Catch errors into an error state and render a message; disable the Reindex button while it runs.

posted.title: Missing alias target crashes with Errno::ENOENT
posted.details:
**What's wrong:** The tsconfig-alias branch of `resolve` returns a path without checking that the file exists, and without the `.ts`/`.tsx` fallback the relative branch has. `File.read` in `constant_value` then raises a raw `Errno::ENOENT` instead of the intended `Search::UnresolvedConstant`.

**When it happens:** Any `paths` entry whose target is missing, extension-less, or a wildcard — e.g. `"@app/flags": ["app/javascript/flags"]` — makes the route indexing crash with an unrelated system error.

**Fix:** Apply the same existence/extension check in the alias branch:

```ruby
target = aliases[spec]&.first
base = target && File.expand_path(target, File.dirname(tsconfig_path))
base && [base, *EXTENSIONS.map { |ext| "#{base}#{ext}" }].find { |c| File.exist?(c) }
```
